title: Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions
excerpt: Practical tips for how to run efficient sessions that get the most value from every token.
content_html:
Input and output tokens

A request goes through the GPU in two phases, and they cost different amounts. 

First, during prefill, the model reads your request and context: the system prompt, your CLAUDE.md, your message, and everything that's been added to the conversation since (the files Claude has read and the output of the commands it ran). Those are your input tokens.

Then, during decode, it writes output tokens: its thinking, the tool calls it makes, and the text you see. This happens one token at a time; a 200-token response is 200 runs of the model, one after the other. Per token, decode keeps the GPU busy for a lot longer, which is why output is priced at roughly 5x input.

A lot of the output tokens in a session are thinking tokens, and how much thinking the model does per turn is what the effort level controls. Like the model, the level you pick with /effort sticks around as your default for the next session too.

Tip: run /model and /effort once in a fresh session to see what you're actually on. Both remember whatever you picked last time, and you want that decision to be deliberate.
Tip: if you already know a session is going to be grunt work, MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 claude turns thinking off for that one session (except on Fable 5), which is the step below /effort low.

Prompt caching

If a request starts with exactly the same tokens as a request the server just saw, the state for that shared beginning comes out the same, so the server can keep it around from last time and only prefill whatever comes after it. This is called prompt caching.

Reading from the cache costs 0.1x the input price, because the server loads the state instead of computing it. Writing tokens into the cache costs a bit more than normal input, up to 2x, since the server also has to hold on to the state afterwards. But the write happens once per token, and the 0.1x reads happen on every turn after it.

Claude Code manages the prompt cache on every request, there's nothing to turn on. However you can break it, so it's important to know how to avoid these cost spikes.

Say we type "fix the failing test in utils.test.ts". Here's what Claude Code sends for it:

  1. Claude Code assembles the first request out of the system prompt (tool definitions included), your CLAUDE.md, and your message, and sends it off (input tokens). Nothing is in the cache yet, so all of it gets prefilled and written into the cache.
  1. The model can't fix a test it hasn't seen, so it thinks for a moment and responds with a Read call for utils.test.ts (output tokens). Claude Code reads the file, appends it to the conversation, and sends the whole thing again (input tokens). This time everything from request 1 is read back out of the cache at a tenth of the price, and the only thing prefilled at full price is what's new: the Read call and the file.
  1. Now the model wants the file under test (output). Another Read, another append, and everything goes out again: requests 1 and 2 from the cache, the second file at full price (input).
  1. The model responds with an Edit (output). Claude Code applies it, appends the result, and sends everything again. Same story: the Edit and its result are new, everything in front of them is a cache read (input).
  1. The model runs npm test (output). Claude Code appends the test output and sends everything again, with the test output as the only new part (input).
  1. The tests pass, and the model responds with a short summary (output). No tool call means nothing to append and no request 6, so we're done.

That's five requests for one small fix, and every one of them contained the entire conversation up to that point. A typical turn is lopsided: tens of thousands of tokens going in, a few hundred coming out. But only what's new in that turn gets prefilled at full price. 

That's the whole per-turn bill: cache reads on the history, full input price on whatever's new, and the output price on the response.

This applies on a subscription too. You don't see these prices directly, but the same requests are what draw down your limits.

The cache has to match from the very start of the request forward, and requests always go out in the same order: tool definitions, then the system prompt, then the conversation (with CLAUDE.md at the front of it). 

If anything in that prefix changes, everything behind it gets prefilled again. A tool result appended to the end of the conversation is the ideal case, since nothing is behind it. What throws the cache away is anything that changes the request further towards the front, or changes what the cache is keyed on:

  • /model: every model has its own cache, so on the next turn the entire conversation gets prefilled again at full price. (This includes opusplan, which switches models every time you go in or out of plan mode.)
  • /effort: the effort level is part of what the cache is keyed on too, so it's the same story. It's why both /model and /effort ask you to confirm when you switch in the middle of a conversation.
  • Fast mode: also part of the key, and the re-prefill happens at fast mode prices, so if you're going to turn it on, turn it on at the start. (Turning it off again is free, cache-wise.)
  • /compact: the conversation gets replaced with a shorter one, so nothing in it matches anymore (the system prompt in front of it survives). Writing the summary itself is cheap as long as the old conversation is still in the cache, so it's a lot cheaper before a long break than after one.
  • Time: every turn resets the clock, but the cache expires after an hour on a subscription or five minutes on an API key (ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 makes it an hour). Come back later than that, and the next turn prefills the whole conversation again. Resuming an old session almost always does too: the cache is usually gone by then, and the system prompt gets rebuilt at launch anyway.

None of this means you should never switch models or effort. It means there are cheap moments to do it, the start of a session or right after a /clear, and expensive ones, the middle of a long conversation.

Tip: if the last few turns went somewhere you don't want to keep, /rewind to just before them instead of running /compact. Rewinding only cuts those turns off the end, so everything before them is still cached and it costs nothing. Compacting rewrites the whole conversation, so it always costs something.

What decides how many tokens a session sends

The main thing to know here is that nothing gets sent just once. Everything that ends up in the conversation, a file Claude read or the output of a command it ran, gets sent again on every turn after it, for the rest of the session. 

It's cached, so each of those re-sends is cheap, but cheap isn't nothing, and it's taking up room in the context the model has to think around on every turn too.

That's really the whole cost model of a session: how many tokens end up in the context, how many turns they stay there, and how many contexts you're running at the same time.

What ends up in the context

Part of what's in the context is there before you type anything: the tool definitions, the system prompt, CLAUDE.md, and whatever else gets loaded at startup.

Tip: run /context in a fresh session to see what's in there before you've typed anything. Keep CLAUDE.md to specific instructions and move workflow-specific ones into skills, which only get loaded when they're used. If there's an MCP server you don't need in this session, turn it off with /mcp.

Nearly everything else that gets added during the session is tool results: the files Claude reads, and the output of the commands it runs.

How much Claude reads mostly comes down to how much it has to figure out on its own. If you say "the tests are failing", it first has to find out which tests: a grep or two, a few files opened to see which one is relevant, and all of those results stay in the context long after they've stopped being useful. 

"Fix the failing test in utils.test.ts" skips the searching and costs one Read call for the file, and "Fix the failing test in @utils.test.ts" doesn't cost the Read call either.

Tip: when you're referring to a file, @-mention it instead of typing the path. Claude Code attaches the file to your message before anything gets sent, so it's in the very first request and there's no Read call for it. The file itself takes up the same room in the context either way, so you only need to mention it once per conversation: it stays there, and @-mentioning it again on a later turn generally attaches a second copy.

The other thing that fills up the context is the output of the commands Claude runs. Every time it runs your tests, a build, or a git log, whatever that prints gets appended to the conversation just like a file it read, and stays there for the same number of turns.

Really big outputs are actually fine: after 30,000 characters Claude Code writes the output to a file and only puts a short preview and the path in the conversation (BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH if you want to change it). 

The problem is everything under that. A test runner that prints 400 passing tests one line at a time comes in under the limit, and those 400 lines are now part of every remaining turn. 

Claude will often take care of this for you with flags and tail, and if you'd rather not leave it up to Claude, there's a small hook in the docs that rewrites noisy commands before they run so only the lines that matter come back.

Tip: put the two or three commands you run all day in CLAUDE.md, quiet flags included, the way you'd type them yourself ("run a single test file with npx vitest run <file> --reporter=dot"). It's a small addition, but it saves a turn and a few hundred lines of output in every session after it.

How many turns it stays there

One long session costs more than the same work spread over a few short ones, and by more than you'd think, because turn 40 is also re-reading the 39 turns before it. You want the context in your session to be short and relevant, so don't carry one task's context into the next: /clear when you start something new, and /compact when the earlier part of the same task is done.

Tip: /rename before you /clear if you'll want the session back later. When you /compact, tell it what to keep, or put a "Compact instructions" section in CLAUDE.md if it's always the same thing. And if you're on a 1M model and would rather have the auto-compact safety net where it used to be, /autocompact 200k puts it back (needs Claude Code v2.1.221+).

Keep an eye on turns that happen when you're not typing, too. A /loop fires as a full turn in the session you set it up in, carrying that whole conversation with it every time, and if it's been more than an hour since the last turn, it's a cache miss on top. Start a fresh session in another terminal and run the loop from there.

Subagents

The other way to keep something out of your context is to have it happen in a different one, which is what subagents are for. A subagent gets its own context window, with its own system prompt, the tools, and your CLAUDE.md, but not your conversation. It runs its own turns, and the only thing that comes back to the main session is its answer. Everything else is thrown away once it's done.

The downside of not having your conversation is that a subagent sometimes has to re-read things the main session already had, and it's paying for its own turns while it does. For a small job it's just overhead. 

It pays off when a job produces a lot of output you don't need to keep, like going through a log. Claude will often reach for one on its own for that kind of thing, and you can ask for one directly when it doesn't ("go through this log in a subagent"). Just keep in mind that the main session only gets back what the subagent chose to report.

Tip: if there's a noisy job you hand off over and over, give it a subagent definition of its own with model: haiku (or sonnet). Otherwise it runs on whatever your main session is running on.

sentences.zh: 以下是 Claude Code 发送的内容：

blocks.html_en: • Claude Code assembles the first request out of the system prompt (tool definitions included), your CLAUDE.md, and your message, and sends it off (input tokens). Nothing is in the cache yet, so all of it gets prefilled and written into the cache.

sentences.en: Claude Code assembles the first request out of the system prompt (tool definitions included), your CLAUDE.md, and your message, and sends it off (input tokens).
sentences.zh: Claude Code 会根据系统提示（包括工具定义）、您的 CLAUDE.md 和您的消息组装第一个请求，并将其发送出去（输入令牌）。

sentences.en: Nothing is in the cache yet, so all of it gets prefilled and written into the cache.
sentences.zh: 缓存中还没有任何内容，因此所有内容都会被预填充并写入缓存中。

blocks.html_en: • The model can't fix a test it hasn't seen, so it thinks for a moment and responds with a Read call for utils.test.ts (output tokens). Claude Code reads the file, appends it to the conversation, and sends the whole thing again (input tokens). This time everything from request 1 is read back out of the cache at a tenth of the price, and the only thing prefilled at full price is what's new: the Read call and the file.

sentences.en: The model can't fix a test it hasn't seen, so it thinks for a moment and responds with a Read call for utils.test.ts (output tokens).
sentences.zh: 该模型无法修复它未见过的测试，因此它会思考一会儿并通过对 utils.test.ts（输出令牌）的 Read 调用进行响应。

sentences.en: Claude Code reads the file, appends it to the conversation, and sends the whole thing again (input tokens).
sentences.zh: Claude Code 读取该文件，将其附加到对话中，然后再次发送整个内容（输入令牌）。

sentences.en: This time everything from request 1 is read back out of the cache at a tenth of the price, and the only thing prefilled at full price is what's new: the Read call and the file.
sentences.zh: 这次，请求 1 中的所有内容都会以十分之一的价格从缓存中读回，唯一以全价预填充的是新内容：Read 调用和文件。

blocks.html_en: • Now the model wants the file under test (output). Another Read, another append, and everything goes out again: requests 1 and 2 from the cache, the second file at full price (input).

sentences.en: Now the model wants the file under test (output).
sentences.zh: 现在模型需要测试文件（输出）。

sentences.en: Another Read, another append, and everything goes out again: requests 1 and 2 from the cache, the second file at full price (input).
sentences.zh: 另一次读取，另一次追加，一切都再次发生：从缓存请求 1 和 2，第二个文件以全价（输入）。

blocks.html_en: • The model responds with an Edit (output). Claude Code applies it, appends the result, and sends everything again. Same story: the Edit and its result are new, everything in front of them is a cache read (input).

sentences.en: The model responds with an Edit (output).
sentences.zh: 模型以编辑（输出）作为响应。

sentences.en: Claude Code applies it, appends the result, and sends everything again.
sentences.zh: Claude Code 应用它，附加结果，然后再次发送所有内容。

sentences.en: Same story: the Edit and its result are new, everything in front of them is a cache read (input).
sentences.zh: 同样的故事：编辑及其结果都是新的，它们前面的所有内容都是缓存读取（输入）。

blocks.html_en: • The model runs npm test (output). Claude Code appends the test output and sends everything again, with the test output as the only new part (input).

sentences.en: The model runs npm test (output).
sentences.zh: 该模型运行 npm test（输出）。

sentences.en: Claude Code appends the test output and sends everything again, with the test output as the only new part (input).
sentences.zh: Claude Code 附加测试输出并再次发送所有内容，测试输出作为唯一的新部分（输入）。

blocks.html_en: • The tests pass, and the model responds with a short summary (output). No tool call means nothing to append and no request 6, so we're done.

sentences.en: The tests pass, and the model responds with a short summary (output).
sentences.zh: 测试通过，模型响应一个简短的摘要（输出）。

sentences.en: No tool call means nothing to append and no request 6, so we're done.
sentences.zh: 没有工具调用意味着没有任何附加内容，也没有请求 6，所以我们就完成了。

blocks.html_en: That's five requests for one small fix, and every one of them contained the entire conversation up to that point. A typical turn is lopsided: tens of thousands of tokens going in, a few hundred coming out. But only what's new in that turn gets prefilled at full price.

sentences.en: That's five requests for one small fix, and every one of them contained the entire conversation up to that point.
sentences.zh: 这是针对一个小修复的五个请求，每个请求都包含了截至该点的整个对话。

sentences.en: A typical turn is lopsided: tens of thousands of tokens going in, a few hundred coming out.
sentences.zh: 典型的转向是不平衡的：数以万计的代币进入，几百个代币出来。

sentences.en: But only what's new in that turn gets prefilled at full price.
sentences.zh: 但只有新推出的产品才会以全价预装。

blocks.html_en: That's the whole per-turn bill: cache reads on the history, full input price on whatever's new, and the output price on the response.

sentences.en: That's the whole per-turn bill: cache reads on the history, full input price on whatever's new, and the output price on the response.
sentences.zh: 这就是每回合的全部费用：历史记录的缓存读取、新内容的完整输入价格以及响应的输出价格。

blocks.html_en: This applies on a subscription too. You don't see these prices directly, but the same requests are what draw down your limits.

sentences.en: This applies on a subscription too.
sentences.zh: 这也适用于订阅。

sentences.en: You don't see these prices directly, but the same requests are what draw down your limits.
sentences.zh: 您无法直接看到这些价格，但相同的请求会降低您的限额。

blocks.html_en: The cache has to match from the very start of the request forward, and requests always go out in the same order: tool definitions, then the system prompt, then the conversation (with CLAUDE.md at the front of it).

sentences.en: The cache has to match from the very start of the request forward, and requests always go out in the same order: tool definitions, then the system prompt, then the conversation (with CLAUDE.md at the front of it).
sentences.zh: 缓存必须从请求转发的一开始就匹配，并且请求始终以相同的顺序发出：工具定义，然后是系统提示，然后是对话（前面有 CLAUDE.md）。

blocks.html_en: If anything in that prefix changes, everything behind it gets prefilled again. A tool result appended to the end of the conversation is the ideal case, since nothing is behind it. What throws the cache away is anything that changes the request further towards the front, or changes what the cache is keyed on:

sentences.en: If anything in that prefix changes, everything behind it gets prefilled again.
sentences.zh: 如果该前缀中的任何内容发生变化，则其后面的所有内容都会再次预先填充。

sentences.en: A tool result appended to the end of the conversation is the ideal case, since nothing is behind it.
sentences.zh: 附加到对话末尾的工具结果是理想的情况，因为其背后没有任何内容。

sentences.en: What throws the cache away is anything that changes the request further towards the front, or changes what the cache is keyed on:
sentences.zh: 丢弃缓存的是任何进一步改变请求的方式，或者改变缓存的关键内容：

blocks.html_en: • /model: every model has its own cache, so on the next turn the entire conversation gets prefilled again at full price. (This includes opusplan, which switches models every time you go in or out of plan mode.)

sentences.en: /model: every model has its own cache, so on the next turn the entire conversation gets prefilled again at full price.
sentences.zh: /model：每个模型都有自己的缓存，因此在下一个回合，整个对话将再次以全价预填充。

sentences.en: (This includes opusplan, which switches models every time you go in or out of plan mode.)
sentences.zh: （这包括 opusplan，它会在您每次进入或退出计划模式时切换模型。）

blocks.html_en: • /effort: the effort level is part of what the cache is keyed on too, so it's the same story. It's why both /model and /effort ask you to confirm when you switch in the middle of a conversation.

sentences.en: /effort: the effort level is part of what the cache is keyed on too, so it's the same story.
sentences.zh: /effort：工作量级别也是缓存所关注的一部分，所以这是同样的故事。

sentences.en: It's why both /model and /effort ask you to confirm when you switch in the middle of a conversation.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么 /model 和 /effort 在您在对话中切换时都会要求您确认。

blocks.html_en: • Fast mode: also part of the key, and the re-prefill happens at fast mode prices, so if you're going to turn it on, turn it on at the start. (Turning it off again is free, cache-wise.)

sentences.en: Fast mode: also part of the key, and the re-prefill happens at fast mode prices, so if you're going to turn it on, turn it on at the start.
sentences.zh: 快速模式：也是密钥的一部分，重新​​预充值以快速模式价格进行，因此如果您要打开它，请在开始时打开它。

sentences.en: (Turning it off again is free, cache-wise.)
sentences.zh: （再次关闭它是免费的，就缓存而言。）

blocks.html_en: • /compact: the conversation gets replaced with a shorter one, so nothing in it matches anymore (the system prompt in front of it survives). Writing the summary itself is cheap as long as the old conversation is still in the cache, so it's a lot cheaper before a long break than after one.

sentences.en: /compact: the conversation gets replaced with a shorter one, so nothing in it matches anymore (the system prompt in front of it survives).
sentences.zh: /compact：对话被替换为较短的对话，因此其中不再匹配任何内容（其前面的系统提示符仍然存在）。

sentences.en: Writing the summary itself is cheap as long as the old conversation is still in the cache, so it's a lot cheaper before a long break than after one.
sentences.zh: 只要旧对话仍在缓存中，编写摘要本身就很便宜，因此在长时间休息之前比长时间休息之后要便宜得多。

blocks.html_en: • Time: every turn resets the clock, but the cache expires after an hour on a subscription or five minutes on an API key (ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 makes it an hour). Come back later than that, and the next turn prefills the whole conversation again. Resuming an old session almost always does too: the cache is usually gone by then, and the system prompt gets rebuilt at launch anyway.

sentences.en: Time: every turn resets the clock, but the cache expires after an hour on a subscription or five minutes on an API key (ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 makes it an hour).
sentences.zh: 时间：每回合都会重置时钟，但缓存会在订阅一小时或 API 密钥五分钟后过期（ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 使其为一小时）。

sentences.en: Come back later than that, and the next turn prefills the whole conversation again.
sentences.zh: 晚一点回来，下一个回合又会再次填充整个对话。

sentences.en: Resuming an old session almost always does too: the cache is usually gone by then, and the system prompt gets rebuilt at launch anyway.
sentences.zh: 恢复旧会话几乎总是会这样做：那时缓存通常已经消失，并且系统提示符无论如何都会在启动时重建。

blocks.html_en: None of this means you should never switch models or effort. It means there are cheap moments to do it, the start of a session or right after a /clear, and expensive ones, the middle of a long conversation.

sentences.en: None of this means you should never switch models or effort.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你永远不应该改变模型或努力。

sentences.en: It means there are cheap moments to do it, the start of a session or right after a /clear, and expensive ones, the middle of a long conversation.
sentences.zh: 这意味着有一些便宜的时刻可以做到这一点，例如会话开始或在 /clear 之后，而昂贵的时刻则可以是在长时间对话的中间。

blocks.html_en: Tip: if the last few turns went somewhere you don't want to keep, /rewind to just before them instead of running /compact. Rewinding only cuts those turns off the end, so everything before them is still cached and it costs nothing. Compacting rewrites the whole conversation, so it always costs something.

sentences.en: Tip: if the last few turns went somewhere you don't want to keep, /rewind to just before them instead of running /compact.
sentences.zh: 提示：如果最后几圈转到您不想保留的地方，请 /rewind 到它们之前，而不是运行 /compact。

sentences.en: Rewinding only cuts those turns off the end, so everything before them is still cached and it costs nothing.
sentences.zh: 倒带只会切断结尾处的那些转弯，因此它们之前的所有内容仍然会被缓存，而且不需要任何成本。

sentences.en: Compacting rewrites the whole conversation, so it always costs something.
sentences.zh: 压缩会重写整个对话，因此总是要付出一些代价。

blocks.html_en: What decides how many tokens a session sends

sentences.en: What decides how many tokens a session sends
sentences.zh: 什么决定了会话发送多少令牌

blocks.html_en: The main thing to know here is that nothing gets sent just once. Everything that ends up in the conversation, a file Claude read or the output of a command it ran, gets sent again on every turn after it, for the rest of the session.

sentences.en: The main thing to know here is that nothing gets sent just once.
sentences.zh: 这里要知道的主要事情是，没有任何内容只会发送一次。

sentences.en: Everything that ends up in the conversation, a file Claude read or the output of a command it ran, gets sent again on every turn after it, for the rest of the session.
sentences.zh: 在对话中结束的所有内容，克劳德读取的文件或运行的命令的输出，都会在会话的其余部分中每回合再次发送。

blocks.html_en: It's cached, so each of those re-sends is cheap, but cheap isn't nothing, and it's taking up room in the context the model has to think around on every turn too.

sentences.en: It's cached, so each of those re-sends is cheap, but cheap isn't nothing, and it's taking up room in the context the model has to think around on every turn too.
sentences.zh: 它被缓存了，所以每次重新发送都很便宜，但便宜并不是什么都没有，而且它在模型也必须在每个回合都考虑的上下文中占用了空间。

blocks.html_en: That's really the whole cost model of a session: how many tokens end up in the context, how many turns they stay there, and how many contexts you're running at the same time.

sentences.en: That's really the whole cost model of a session: how many tokens end up in the context, how many turns they stay there, and how many contexts you're running at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是会话的整个成本模型：有多少令牌最终出现在上下文中，它们在那里停留了多少轮，以及同时运行了多少个上下文。

blocks.html_en: What ends up in the context

sentences.en: What ends up in the context
sentences.zh: 在上下文中最终会发生什么

blocks.html_en: Part of what's in the context is there before you type anything: the tool definitions, the system prompt, CLAUDE.md, and whatever else gets loaded at startup.

sentences.en: Part of what's in the context is there before you type anything: the tool definitions, the system prompt, CLAUDE.md, and whatever else gets loaded at startup.
sentences.zh: 上下文中的部分内容在您键入任何内容之前就已存在：工具定义、系统提示符、CLAUDE.md 以及启动时加载的任何其他内容。

blocks.html_en: Tip: run /context in a fresh session to see what's in there before you've typed anything. Keep CLAUDE.md to specific instructions and move workflow-specific ones into skills, which only get loaded when they're used. If there's an MCP server you don't need in this session, turn it off with /mcp.

sentences.en: Tip: run /context in a fresh session to see what's in there before you've typed anything.
sentences.zh: 提示：在输入任何内容之前，在新会话中运行 /context 以查看其中的内容。

sentences.en: Keep CLAUDE.md to specific instructions and move workflow-specific ones into skills, which only get loaded when they're used.
sentences.zh: 将 CLAUDE.md 保留为特定指令，并将特定于工作流程的指令移至技能中，这些指令仅在使用时才会加载。

sentences.en: If there's an MCP server you don't need in this session, turn it off with /mcp.
sentences.zh: 如果此会话中不需要 MCP 服务器，请使用 /mcp 将其关闭。

blocks.html_en: Nearly everything else that gets added during the session is tool results: the files Claude reads, and the output of the commands it runs.

sentences.en: Nearly everything else that gets added during the session is tool results: the files Claude reads, and the output of the commands it runs.
sentences.zh: 会话期间添加的几乎所有其他内容都是工具结果：Claude 读取的文件以及它运行的命令的输出。

blocks.html_en: How much Claude reads mostly comes down to how much it has to figure out on its own. If you say "the tests are failing", it first has to find out which tests: a grep or two, a few files opened to see which one is relevant, and all of those results stay in the context long after they've stopped being useful.

sentences.en: How much Claude reads mostly comes down to how much it has to figure out on its own.
sentences.zh: 克劳德读了多少书，主要取决于它必须自己弄清楚多少。

sentences.en: If you say "the tests are failing", it first has to find out which tests: a grep or two, a few files opened to see which one is relevant, and all of those results stay in the context long after they've stopped being useful.
sentences.zh: 如果你说“测试失败了”，它首先必须找出哪些测试：一两个 grep，打开一些文件以查看哪个是相关的，并且所有这些结果在它们不再有用之后很长时间仍保留在上下文中。

blocks.html_en: "Fix the failing test in utils.test.ts" skips the searching and costs one Read call for the file, and "Fix the failing test in @utils.test.ts" doesn't cost the Read call either.

sentences.en: "Fix the failing test in utils.test.ts" skips the searching and costs one Read call for the file, and "Fix the failing test in @utils.test.ts" doesn't cost the Read call either.
sentences.zh: “修复 utils.test.ts 中的失败测试”会跳过搜索并花费一次对该文件的 Read 调用，而“修复 @utils.test.ts 中的失败测试”也不花费 Read 调用。

blocks.html_en: Tip: when you're referring to a file, @-mention it instead of typing the path. Claude Code attaches the file to your message before anything gets sent, so it's in the very first request and there's no Read call for it. The file itself takes up the same room in the context either way, so you only need to mention it once per conversation: it stays there, and @-mentioning it again on a later turn generally attaches a second copy.

sentences.en: Tip: when you're referring to a file, @-mention it instead of typing the path.
sentences.zh: 提示：当您引用文件时，请使用 @ 提及它，而不是键入路径。

sentences.en: Claude Code attaches the file to your message before anything gets sent, so it's in the very first request and there's no Read call for it.
sentences.zh: Claude Code 在发送任何内容之前将文件附加到您的消息中，因此它位于第一个请求中，并且没有对其进行 Read 调用。

sentences.en: The file itself takes up the same room in the context either way, so you only need to mention it once per conversation: it stays there, and @-mentioning it again on a later turn generally attaches a second copy.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，文件本身都会在上下文中占用相同的空间，因此每次对话只需提及一次：它会保留在那里，并且在稍后的回合中再次@提及它通常会附加第二个副本。

blocks.html_en: The other thing that fills up the context is the output of the commands Claude runs. Every time it runs your tests, a build, or a git log, whatever that prints gets appended to the conversation just like a file it read, and stays there for the same number of turns.

sentences.en: The other thing that fills up the context is the output of the commands Claude runs.
sentences.zh: 填充上下文的另一件事是 Claude 运行的命令的输出。

sentences.en: Every time it runs your tests, a build, or a git log, whatever that prints gets appended to the conversation just like a file it read, and stays there for the same number of turns.
sentences.zh: 每次它运行测试、构建或 git 日志时，打印的任何内容都会像它读取的文件一样附加到对话中，并在那里停留相同的轮数。

blocks.html_en: Really big outputs are actually fine: after 30,000 characters Claude Code writes the output to a file and only puts a short preview and the path in the conversation (BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH if you want to change it).

sentences.en: Really big outputs are actually fine: after 30,000 characters Claude Code writes the output to a file and only puts a short preview and the path in the conversation (BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH if you want to change it).
sentences.zh: 真正大的输出实际上很好：在 30,000 个字符之后，Claude Code 将输出写入文件，并且只在对话中放置简短的预览和路径（如果您想更改它，则为 BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH）。

blocks.html_en: The problem is everything under that. A test runner that prints 400 passing tests one line at a time comes in under the limit, and those 400 lines are now part of every remaining turn.

sentences.en: The problem is everything under that.
sentences.zh: 问题在于这一切。

sentences.en: A test runner that prints 400 passing tests one line at a time comes in under the limit, and those 400 lines are now part of every remaining turn.
sentences.zh: 一次一行打印 400 个通过测试的测试运行程序低于限制，而这 400 行现在是每个剩余回合的一部分。

blocks.html_en: Claude will often take care of this for you with flags and tail, and if you'd rather not leave it up to Claude, there's a small hook in the docs that rewrites noisy commands before they run so only the lines that matter come back.

sentences.en: Claude will often take care of this for you with flags and tail, and if you'd rather not leave it up to Claude, there's a small hook in the docs that rewrites noisy commands before they run so only the lines that matter come back.
sentences.zh: Claude 通常会用 flags 和 tail 为你处理这个问题，如果你不想把它留给 Claude，文档中有一个小钩子，可以在运行之前重写嘈杂的命令，这样只有重要的行才会返回。

blocks.html_en: Tip: put the two or three commands you run all day in CLAUDE.md, quiet flags included, the way you'd type them yourself ("run a single test file with npx vitest run <file> --reporter=dot"). It's a small addition, but it saves a turn and a few hundred lines of output in every session after it.

sentences.en: Tip: put the two or three commands you run all day in CLAUDE.md, quiet flags included, the way you'd type them yourself ("run a single test file with npx vitest run <file> --reporter=dot").
sentences.zh: 提示：将您整天运行的两到三个命令放入 CLAUDE.md 中，包括安静标志，按照您自己键入的方式（“使用 npx vitest run <file> --reporter=dot 运行单个测试文件”）。

sentences.en: It's a small addition, but it saves a turn and a few hundred lines of output in every session after it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很小的添加，但它节省了一个回合，并在之后的每个会话中节省了几百行输出。

blocks.html_en: How many turns it stays there

sentences.en: How many turns it stays there
sentences.zh: 在那里转了多少圈

blocks.html_en: One long session costs more than the same work spread over a few short ones, and by more than you'd think, because turn 40 is also re-reading the 39 turns before it. You want the context in your session to be short and relevant, so don't carry one task's context into the next: /clear when you start something new, and /compact when the earlier part of the same task is done.

sentences.en: One long session costs more than the same work spread over a few short ones, and by more than you'd think, because turn 40 is also re-reading the 39 turns before it.
sentences.zh: 一个长会话的成本比分散在几个短会话中的相同工作要多，而且比你想象的要多，因为第 40 回合还需要重新阅读之前的 39 回合。

content_html_zh:
输入和输出令牌

一个请求分两个阶段通过 GPU，它们的成本不同。

首先，在预填充期间，模型读取您的请求和上下文：系统提示符、您的 CLAUDE.md、您的消息以及此后添加到对话中的所有内容（Claude 已读取的文件及其运行的命令的输出）。 这些是您的输入令牌。

然后，在解码过程中，它会写入输出标记：它的想法、工具调用它所做的以及您看到的文本。 这种情况一次只发生一个标记； 200 个令牌的响应是模型的 200 次运行，一次又一次。 对于每个令牌，解码会使 GPU 忙碌的时间更长，这就是为什么输出的定价约为输入的 5 倍。

会话中的许多输出令牌都是思考令牌，模型每轮思考的次数是努力级别控制的。 与模型一样，您使用 /effort 选择的级别也将作为下一个会话的默认级别。

提示：在新会话中运行 /model 和 /effort 一次，看看您实际在做什么。 双方都会记得你上次选择的任何内容，并且你希望这个决定是经过深思熟虑的。
提示：如果您已经知道某个会话将是一项繁重的工作，则 MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 克劳德会关闭该会话的思考（寓言 5 除外），这是低于 /effort low 的步骤。

提示缓存

如果请求以与服务器刚刚看到的请求完全相同的令牌开头，则该共享开头的状态将相同，因此服务器可以保留上次的令牌，并且仅预填充其后的内容。 这称为提示缓存。

从缓存读取的成本是输入价格的 0.1 倍，因为服务器加载状态而不是计算状态。 将令牌写入缓存的成本比正常输入高一些，最高可达 2 倍，因为服务器之后还必须保留状态。 但是每个令牌都会写入一次，并且在其之后的每一轮都会发生 0.1x 读取。

Claude Code 管理每个请求的提示缓存，无需打开任何内容。 但是，您可能会破坏它，因此了解如何避免这些成本飙升非常重要。

假设我们输入“修复 utils.test.ts 中失败的测试”。 以下是 Claude Code 发送的内容：

  1. Claude Code 会根据系统提示（包括工具定义）、您的 CLAUDE.md 和您的消息组装第一个请求，并将其发送出去（输入令牌）。 缓存中还没有任何内容，因此所有内容都会被预填充并写入缓存中。
  1. 该模型无法修复它未见过的测试，因此它会思考一会儿并通过对 utils.test.ts（输出令牌）的 Read 调用进行响应。 Claude Code 读取该文件，将其附加到对话中，然后再次发送整个内容（输入令牌）。 这次，请求 1 中的所有内容都会以十分之一的价格从缓存中读回，唯一以全价预填充的是新内容：Read 调用和文件。
  1. 现在模型需要测试文件（输出）。 另一次读取，另一次追加，一切都再次发生：从缓存请求 1 和 2，第二个文件以全价（输入）。
  1. 模型以编辑（输出）作为响应。 Claude Code 应用它，附加结果，然后再次发送所有内容。 同样的故事：编辑及其结果都是新的，它们前面的所有内容都是缓存读取（输入）。
  1. 该模型运行 npm test（输出）。 Claude Code 附加测试输出并再次发送所有内容，测试输出作为唯一的新部分（输入）。
  1. 测试通过，模型响应一个简短的摘要（输出）。 没有工具调用意味着没有任何附加内容，也没有请求 6，所以我们就完成了。

这是针对一个小修复的五个请求，每个请求都包含了截至该点的整个对话。 典型的转向是不平衡的：数以万计的代币进入，几百个代币出来。 但只有新推出的产品才会以全价预装。

这就是每回合的全部费用：历史记录的缓存读取、新内容的完整输入价格以及响应的输出价格。

这也适用于订阅。 您无法直接看到这些价格，但相同的请求会降低您的限额。

缓存必须从请求转发的一开始就匹配，并且请求始终以相同的顺序发出：工具定义，然后是系统提示，然后是对话（前面有 CLAUDE.md）。

如果该前缀中的任何内容发生变化，则其后面的所有内容都会再次预先填充。 附加到对话末尾的工具结果是理想的情况，因为其背后没有任何内容。 丢弃缓存的是任何进一步改变请求的方式，或者改变缓存的关键内容：

  • /model：每个模型都有自己的缓存，因此在下一个回合，整个对话将再次以全价预填充。 （这包括 opusplan，它会在您每次进入或退出计划模式时切换模型。）
  • /effort：工作量级别也是缓存所关注的一部分，所以这是同样的故事。 这就是为什么 /model 和 /effort 在您在对话中切换时都会要求您确认。
  • 快速模式：也是密钥的一部分，重新​​预充值以快速模式价格进行，因此如果您要打开它，请在开始时打开它。 （再次关闭它是免费的，就缓存而言。）
  • /compact：对话被替换为较短的对话，因此其中不再匹配任何内容（其前面的系统提示符仍然存在）。 只要旧对话仍在缓存中，编写摘要本身就很便宜，因此在长时间休息之前比长时间休息之后要便宜得多。
  • 时间：每回合都会重置时钟，但缓存会在订阅一小时或 API 密钥五分钟后过期（ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 使其为一小时）。 晚一点回来，下一个回合又会再次填充整个对话。 恢复旧会话几乎总是会这样做：那时缓存通常已经消失，并且系统提示符无论如何都会在启动时重建。

这并不意味着你永远不应该改变模型或努力。 这意味着有一些便宜的时刻可以做到这一点，例如会话开始或在 /clear 之后，而昂贵的时刻则可以是在长时间对话的中间。

提示：如果最后几圈转到您不想保留的地方，请 /rewind 到它们之前，而不是运行 /compact。 倒带只会切断结尾处的那些转弯，因此它们之前的所有内容仍然会被缓存，而且不需要任何成本。 压缩会重写整个对话，因此总是要付出一些代价。

什么决定了会话发送多少令牌

这里要知道的主要事情是，没有任何内容只会发送一次。 在对话中结束的所有内容，克劳德读取的文件或运行的命令的输出，都会在会话的其余部分中每回合再次发送。

它被缓存了，所以每次重新发送都很便宜，但便宜并不是什么都没有，而且它在模型也必须在每个回合都考虑的上下文中占用了空间。

这实际上是会话的整个成本模型：有多少令牌最终出现在上下文中，它们在那里停留了多少轮，以及同时运行了多少个上下文。

在上下文中最终会发生什么

上下文中的部分内容在您键入任何内容之前就已存在：工具定义、系统提示符、CLAUDE.md 以及启动时加载的任何其他内容。

提示：在输入任何内容之前，在新会话中运行 /context 以查看其中的内容。 将 CLAUDE.md 保留为特定指令，并将特定于工作流程的指令移至技能中，这些指令仅在使用时才会加载。 如果此会话中不需要 MCP 服务器，请使用 /mcp 将其关闭。

会话期间添加的几乎所有其他内容都是工具结果：Claude 读取的文件以及它运行的命令的输出。

克劳德读了多少书，主要取决于它必须自己弄清楚多少。 如果你说“测试失败了”，它首先必须找出哪些测试：一两个 grep，打开一些文件以查看哪个是相关的，并且所有这些结果在它们不再有用之后很长时间仍保留在上下文中。

“修复 utils.test.ts 中的失败测试”会跳过搜索并花费一次对该文件的 Read 调用，而“修复 @utils.test.ts 中的失败测试”也不花费 Read 调用。

提示：当您引用文件时，请使用 @ 提及它，而不是键入路径。 Claude Code 在发送任何内容之前将文件附加到您的消息中，因此它位于第一个请求中，并且没有对其进行 Read 调用。 无论哪种方式，文件本身都会在上下文中占用相同的空间，因此每次对话只需提及一次：它会保留在那里，并且在稍后的回合中再次@提及它通常会附加第二个副本。

填充上下文的另一件事是 Claude 运行的命令的输出。 每次它运行测试、构建或 git 日志时，打印的任何内容都会像它读取的文件一样附加到对话中，并在那里停留相同的轮数。

真正大的输出实际上很好：在 30,000 个字符之后，Claude Code 将输出写入文件，并且只在对话中放置简短的预览和路径（如果您想更改它，则为 BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH）。

问题在于这一切。 一次一行打印 400 个通过测试的测试运行程序低于限制，而这 400 行现在是每个剩余回合的一部分。

Claude 通常会用 flags 和 tail 为你处理这个问题，如果你不想把它留给 Claude，文档中有一个小钩子，可以在运行之前重写嘈杂的命令，这样只有重要的行才会返回。

提示：将您整天运行的两到三个命令放入 CLAUDE.md 中，包括安静标志，按照您自己键入的方式（“使用 npx vitest run <file> --reporter=dot 运行单个测试文件”）。 这是一个很小的添加，但它节省了一个回合，并在之后的每个会话中节省了几百行输出。

在那里转了多少圈

一个长会话的成本比分散在几个短会话中的相同工作要多，而且比你想象的要多，因为第 40 回合还需要重新阅读之前的 39 回合。 您希望会话中的上下文简短且相关，因此不要将一个任务的上下文带入下一个任务：在开始新任务时使用 /clear，在完成同一任务的早期部分时使用 /compact。

提示：如果您希望稍后恢复会话，请先 /rename /clear。 当您 /compact 时，告诉它要保留什么，或者在 CLAUDE.md 中放置一个“紧凑指令”部分（如果它始终是相同的内容）。 如果您使用的是 1M 型号，并且希望将自动紧凑型安全网保留在原来的位置，则 /autocompact 200k 可以将其放回原位（需要 Claude Code v2.1.221+）。

还要留意您不打字时发生的情况。 /循环在您设置的会话中作为一个完整的轮次触发，每次都会携带整个对话，如果自上次轮次以来已经超过一个小时，那么它就是顶部的缓存未命中。 在另一个终端中启动新会话并从那里运行循环。

子代理

另一种将某些事情排除在上下文之外的方法是让它在不同的环境中发生，这就是子代理的用途。 子代理有自己的上下文窗口，有自己的系统提示符、工具和您的 CLAUDE.md，但不是您的对话。 它自己轮流运行，返回主会话的唯一内容就是它的答案。 一旦完成，其他所有东西都会被扔掉。

不进行对话的缺点是，子代理有时必须重新读取主会话已经拥有的内容，并且在这样做时它会为自己的轮次付费。 对于一项小工作来说，这只是开销。

当一项工作产生大量不需要保留的输出（例如查看日志）时，它就会得到回报。 对于此类事情，克劳德经常会自己寻求一个，如果没有，您可以直接要求一个（“在子代理中查看此日志”）。 请记住，主会话仅返回子代理选择报告的内容。

提示：如果您一遍又一遍地移交一项嘈杂的工作，请使用模型给它一个自己的子代理定义：俳句（或十四行诗）。 否则，它会在您的主会话正在运行的任何地方运行。

在上述所有内容中，有四件事值得关注，大致按成本排列：
